objection.quote: If every two members of $\mathcal F$ intersect, then there are finitely many nonempty finite sets $B_1,\ldots,B_s\subseteq P$ such that, for every finite $X\subseteq P$,
objection.witness: The Lemma is false. Take C={c1,c2} and F={C}∪{{c2}∪g : g∈G}, which is pairwise intersecting for any family G of finite sets. Its finite transversals avoiding c2 are {c1}∪(transversal of G), and a family G of finite sets can have infinitely many pairwise-incomparable minimal finite transversals, so no finite list B_1,...,B_s exists.
